messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT PAGER: SEV-2 - us-east inference pool 'gpu-pool-4' reporting sustained queue growth and 5xxs. Autoscaler hit max_replicas; throttling observed. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:
ellie (oncall): I'm on it. what's the customer impact? any single-customer spike?
ops-bot: Affected routes: /v1/stream-generation, /v1/embeddings-us-east. Queue depth ~62k across the pool, 503s rising. Some customers reporting timeouts. logs: `autoscaler: scale_attempt failed: max_replicas reached`
samir: digging in metrics now. GPU util at node-level ~70-95%, but there are free MIG slices reported. Looks like fragmentation: many nodes have small MIG slices free but not contiguous capacity for the high-memory models.
maya (sre): Confirmed: `nvidia-smi mig -l` shows many small slices available (1g/4gb), but our scheduler requests `gpus: 12gb contiguous` for the large embeddings jobs. Binpacking can't fit them.
ellie (oncall): so autoscaler is scaling but can't place pods because of MIG sizing mismatch -> effectively stranded capacity?
samir: correct. autoscaler logs: ```
I0312 20:02:10.123 autoscaler.go:412] pool=gpu-pool-4 attempt scale up to 40 replicas
I0312 20:02:11.456 scheduler.go:89] placement failed: no nodes match resource request {gpu_memory>=12Gi}
```
jamal: what's current and max in the autoscaler? can we bump limits temporarily?
ops-bot: autoscaler status: `current_replicas=40`, `max_replicas=40`, `pending_pods=184`, `scale_cooldown=30s`
ellie (oncall): two immediate mitigation paths: 1) relieve high-memory requests by routing them to fallback model variants with lower memory footprint (cpu or small-gpu) 2) create emergency reallocation: drain low-priority pods and force binpack for contiguous slots. Which is quicker?
maya (sre): fallback variant rollout is quickest for a subset: embeddings can fall back to a quantized model (8GB) with slight quality loss. But some customers (enterprise) pinned to large model; we need manual intervention for them.
samir: we also have a scheduler bug where MIG-aware binpacking prefers spreading across nodes; it should prefer filling nodes to create contiguous free slices. Quick patch: change placement policy to `pack_by_mig_slot` (hotfix) — I can push a config change to the scheduler within 10 minutes.
jamal: do it. Also approve temporary increase of max_replicas to 60? will that help?
ellie (oncall): raising max_replicas helps only if there are nodes with contiguous GPU memory; if fragmentation is the problem, more replicas won't help and could worsen fragmentation.
product-ash: we should notify customers proactively; any list of impacted tenants?
samir: initial list: `acme-payments`, `nano-ai`, `shopwave-pro` show elevated error rates. I'll post a more complete list in 15m.
ops-bot: NOTE: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-fragmentation , playbook step 3 (evacuate low priority) recommended.
ellie (oncall): action items: - samir -> push scheduler pack_by_mig_slot hotfix (10m) - maya -> start fallback routing for non-enterprise embeddings (5m) - jamal -> prepare manual node drains and reboots for aggressive binpack (20m) - ops-bot -> page infra-team for potential node resize (mig profile change)
samir: pushing hotfix now. diff: ```
- scheduling.strategy: spread
+ scheduling.strategy: pack_by_mig_slot
+ scheduling.mig_awareness: true
```
[2m later]
samir: hotfix deployed to scheduler canary (10% of placement traffic). placement failures down ~40% in canary.
maya (sre): fallback routing live for non-enterprise embedding jobs. Queue drain rate improved from 120/s to 260/s for fallbacks.
ellie (oncall): nice. remaining problem: enterprise pinned customers still stuck, queue for them is growing.
jamal: starting manual rebalancer: draining nodes with many small slices and rebooting to consolidate MIG profiles onto larger slices on some nodes. This will cause short interruption to low-priority pods. Executing drain on node gpu-node-57 now: `kubectl drain gpu-node-57 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: customers experiencing > 2x latency for affected routes; SLOs breached for some hosted customers. External status page updated. :fire:
product-ash: schedule call for customer ops? We should offer mitigation: temporary quota increase on dedicated or suggestion to use deduped batch windows.
ellie (oncall): Jamal, coordinate with support for enterprise customer notifications. Samir, continue canary rollout to 50% if canary keeps improving.
samir: canary stable at 10m, pushing to 50%. Also adjusting scheduler heuristic to consider MIG slice coalescing threshold: allow packing pods to split embeddings across two slices if combined capacity >= request (experimental).
maya (sre): rebalancer drained 3 nodes, after reboot nodes came up with larger MIG profiles (consolidated), resulting in ~8 contiguous slots. Scheduler placement success increased. Queue dropping steadily.
ellie (oncall): metrics: queue depth down from 62k -> 18k in 35 minutes, error rate trending down. Customers still affected but improving.
ops-bot: HANDOFF: ellie handing off to jamal for night shift. Last known state: autoscaler max_replicas temporarily bumped to 50 (manual override), scheduler pack_by_mig_slot rolled out to 50%, fallback routing enabled for non-enterprise clients, manual reboots completed on 6 nodes.
jamal: taking over. next steps: finish scheduler rollout to 100%, monitor for regression, run periodic binpack job overnight to reduce fragmentation, coordinate with infra to evaluate long-term changes (standardize MIG profiles, improve autoscaler to be MIG-aware).
ellie (oncall): thanks team. I'll write post-incident notes and customer impact summary. Action item list created: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2711112222/actions (priv). :thumbsup:
